summary: Layer-3 Research Gate for masterplan step 82.5 (exit-quality ratio aggregation blowup). Write-first: the brief is on disk before the envelope returns.

Precise anchors: :999-1001 per-row reads with three `or 0.0` collapses; :1002-1003 `if mae_abs > 0: edge_ratios.append(mfe / mae_abs)` = the silent drop; :1027 leakage rule reads the fabricated 0.0; :1031 edge mean over the mae>0 subset (26 rows); :1032 capture mean over ALL points (32 rows). SECOND, INDEPENDENT COPY of the same mean at backend/services/paper_round_trips.py:157 (feeds /performance -> round_trip_summary). Birth sites of capture_ratio: paper_round_trips.py:97 and paper_trader.py:591, both `... if mfe > 0 else 0.0`.
result.frontend_double_scales: NO. `frontend/src/components/MfeMaeScatter.tsx:114` renders `${(data.summary.avg_capture_ratio * 100).toFixed(0)}%`. capture_ratio = realized_pnl_pct / mfe_pct -- percent divided by percent, so the quantity is DIMENSIONLESS and multiplying by 100 to render a percent is CORRECT. -42.08 x 100 = -4208%, exactly the observed tile. Corroborated three ways in the same file: :111 edge_ratio uses `.toFixed(2)` with NO x100 (bare ratio, matches the reported 86.92); :168 the per-point tooltip uses the same x100; :121 renders the 0.4 threshold as "40%". There is no second defect -- the formatter is handed an already-wrong number. DO NOT change the x100: if the backend later emits a value already in percent, that multiply becomes a real double-scale.
result.recommended_definition:
PER-TRADE capture_ratio (nullable, domain-restricted): None if mfe_pct < MIN_MFE_PCT (=1.0 percentage point), else realized_pnl_pct / mfe_pct. The 1.0pp floor is justified because every published interpretive threshold (0.40 / 0.60 / 0.75) is a fraction of an economically meaningful move; below ~1pp the "available move" sits inside the round-trip cost+noise band (paper_transaction_cost_pct applied twice at paper_trader.py:575). This ONE threshold subsumes both pathologies -- it removes the 8 mfe==0 rows AND 000660.KS at mfe=0.0001. MIN_MFE_PCT is the one free parameter; surface it in the payload.

AGGREGATE capture (the tile): headline = MEDIAN over the defined subset (per-trade estimator, like-for-like with the per-trade literature thresholds). Secondary = ratio-of-sums sum(pnl_pct)/sum(mfe_pct) over the same subset, guarded by denom > 0 else None. Emit n_defined AND n_undefined; the tile must display n_defined, not n_points.

PER-TRADE edge_ratio (extended-real, NEVER dropped): +inf if |mae|==0 and mfe>0 (perfect trade, no adverse excursion); None if |mae|==0 and mfe==0; else mfe_pct/|mae_pct|.

AGGREGATE edge (the tile): headline = MEDIAN over ALL rows with the +inf rows RANKED (not deleted) -- finite whenever <50% of rows are degenerate (19% here). This deletes the `if mae_abs > 0` filter and with it the survivorship bias. If the median itself lands on an +inf row, return None and disclose; never render Infinity. Secondary = sum(mfe)/sum(|mae|) over all rows.

EVERY DEGENERATE CASE: (a) mfe>=1.0, mae<0 -> both numeric; (b) mfe>=1.0, mae==0 -> capture numeric, edge=+inf ranked into the median; (c) 0<mfe<1.0 -> capture None (counted in n_undefined), edge numeric if mae!=0; (d) mfe==0, mae<0 (8 rows) -> capture None, edge = 0.0 (a real, meaningful zero); (e) mfe==0 AND mae==0 -> both None; (f) n_defined==0 -> tile shows "n/a", NOT 0%; (g) sum(mfe)==0 -> ratio-of-sums returns None.

WHY THE ASYMMETRY (the crux, and it answers "exclude vs redefine" differently for each metric): mae==0 means the trade never traded against us -- a genuine, desirable, measurable property, so it must be KEPT (excluding it deletes the BEST trades). mfe==0 means there was no exit decision to grade -- the ENTRY failed -- so including it at a fabricated 0.0 blames the exit for an entry failure, and it must be EXCLUDED. Exclude for capture; redefine for edge.

WHAT THE 32-ROW FIXTURE SHOULD REPORT (predictions -- RE-MEASURE, do not carry forward as asserted values): avg_capture_ratio median ~0.63 and inside [0,1]; exactly 0.63 only if the excluded set is exactly the 8 mfe==0 rows (n_defined=24) -- the 1.0pp floor also removes 000660.KS, which can shift the median by one order statistic. n_defined + n_undefined == 32 exactly. edge median over all 32 with the 6 mae==0 rows ranked at +inf: >= 0.81 and finite, strictly greater than the caller's 0.81 (that was measured over the 26-row surviving subset; re-admitting 6 rows at the top shifts the median up 3 positions). Neither tile may render -4208% or 86.92 under any row ordering.

MUTATION-RESISTANT INVARIANTS: INV1 fixture row {mfe_pct:0.0001, realized_pnl_pct:-0.13} (the real 000660.KS row) must not move the aggregate outside [-3,3] -- reverting :1032 to the mean turns it red. INV2 n_defined+n_undefined==n_points and the edge denominator count == n_points -- restoring `if mae_abs > 0` turns it red. INV3 an all-mfe==0 fixture must return None and render "n/a" -- restoring `else 0.0` turns it red. INV4 deleting the single most extreme row moves each headline by <0.10 (a mean fails by ~40). INV5 /performance and /mfe-mae-scatter must agree on the same trade list -- patching only paper_trading.py turns it red.

CHANGE SITES: paper_round_trips.py:97, :141, :157 (+:159-170 payload); paper_trading.py:1001, :1002-1003, :1027, :1031-1032; paper_trader.py:591; frontend types.ts:766 + api.ts:524 -> `number | null` + presence-discriminating tile (MfeMaeScatter.tsx:111,114,168), keeping the x100; backend/tests/test_paper_trading_v2.py:235-243 (the existing test only asserts key presence and cannot fail on any value).
key_findings: THE MEAN DOES NOT EXIST -- this is not an outlier problem. A ratio whose denominator can reach zero is Cauchy-like; Franz (arXiv:0710.2024, read in full via ar5iv) proves 'Neither the expected value nor the variance exist' and that 'the mean of independent, identically Cauchy-distributed variables follows the SAME Cauchy distribution as each of the individual variables'. So -42.08 is not a bad estimate of a true value -- there is no true value, and collecting more trades will never make it converge. Winsorizing/clipping is equally wrong: it yields a finite number with no population parameter to estimate.

FRONTEND DOES NOT DOUBLE-SCALE (I3 answered plainly). capture_ratio = pnl_pct/mfe_pct is dimensionless, so MfeMaeScatter.tsx:114's x100 is correct; -42.08 x 100 = -4208% exactly. Corroborated by :111 (edge ratio has no x100, matching 86.92), :168 and :121. Single backend-side defect. Do NOT touch the formatter.

mfe == 0 IS A CLAMP ARTEFACT, NOT A MEASUREMENT. paper_trader.py:718-721 seeds prev_mfe from `or 0.0` then takes max(prev_mfe, pnl_pct), so MFE is floored at 0 by construction -- a trade whose best mark was -3% records mfe=0 and the true MFE is unrecoverable. This MATCHES the industry convention (TradingDiaryPro, read in full: 'if the trade ... was never in the profit zone then the MFE is zero'), so it is a domain restriction to respect, not a bug to fix.

THE TWO DEGENERACIES NEED OPPOSITE TREATMENTS. mae==0 (6/32) means the trade never traded against us -- a genuine, desirable property whose edge ratio is +inf; the `if mae_abs > 0` filter at paper_trading.py:1002 therefore DELETES THE BEST TRADES, a survivorship bias with the sign pointing the wrong way. mfe==0 (8/32) means there was no exit decision to grade -- the ENTRY failed -- so including it at a fabricated 0.0 blames the exit. Exclude for capture; keep (rank, don't drop) for edge.

A MEDIAN IS DEFINED OVER THE EXTENDED REALS; A MEAN IS NOT. +inf rows can be ranked instead of deleted, so a median needs no exclusion while fewer than half the rows are degenerate (19% here). The `if mae_abs > 0` filter exists ONLY because the code chose a mean -- fixing the estimator removes the need for the filter.

TWO INDEPENDENT COPIES OF THE SAME BROKEN MEAN, so the fix has two edit sites: paper_trading.py:1031-1032 (the tile) and paper_round_trips.py:157 (feeding /performance -> round_trip_summary.avg_capture_ratio). The second IS open finding 55.3 F-10 ('avg_capture_ratio=-53.7 implausible', filed 2026-06, never fixed). Patching only the endpoint leaves /performance blown up.

SECOND-ORDER DEFECT FROM THE SAME ROOT CAUSE: the leakage rule at paper_trading.py:1027 tests `p['capture_ratio'] < 0.4`, which the fabricated 0.0 ALWAYS satisfies -- so all 8 mfe==0 rows are silently eligible to be flagged 'exit leakers'. The n_leakers tile is contaminated too.

THE TWO TILES ALREADY USE DIFFERENT DENOMINATORS AND DISCLOSE NEITHER: edge_ratio averages over 26 rows (mae>0 subset) while avg_capture averages over all 32, yet the UI shows a single n_points=32 beside both.

THE HOUSE ZERO-DENOMINATOR RULE ALREADY EXISTS AND IS BEING VIOLATED: sovereign_api.py:566-569 -- 'Zero-denominator contract: return None for the ratio, not infinity'. The exit-quality path's `else 0.0` predates it. Same absence-becomes-affirmative class as auto-memory project_fabricated_safe_80_36.

CORRECT AGGREGATION OF A SET OF RATIOS WEIGHTS EACH BY ITS OWN DENOMINATOR -- which is algebraically the ratio of sums (ProcessExcellenceNetwork's weighted-average procedure == Wikipedia's r = sum(y)/sum(x); worked example 8% wrong vs 9.4% right). BUT PMC2430201 (peer-reviewed) warns ratio-of-sums itself degrades when the denominator is 'heavily skewed towards zero', producing 'a high proportion of exceedingly large ratios ... biased to higher values' -- exactly this data (8/32 at exactly 0). So ratio-of-sums is a SECONDARY readout here, never the headline.

NO ROBUST-AGGREGATION HELPER EXISTS IN THE REPO. perf_metrics.py -- the documented single source of truth for metrics -- has no median/trimmed/winsorized estimator. The closest reusable idiom is the hand-rolled median already inside the defective module (paper_round_trips.py:153-154, median_holding_days), plus a hand-rolled P75 already in the endpoint being fixed (paper_trading.py:1022-1025).

PUBLISHED INTERPRETIVE SCALE IS BOUNDED IN [0,1]: <0.40 = noise-driven exits, >0.50 solid, 0.60+ trend setups, 0.65-0.80 well-optimized, >0.75 excellent. -4208% is not a bad score on that scale -- it is off the scale entirely.

RECENCY (2024-2026): two complementary findings plus a decisive NEGATIVE result. arXiv:2403.12110 (2024) ranks robust location estimators (median-of-means / median-Hodges-Lehmann optimal under heavy tails; winsorized less biased than trimmed) -- useful AFTER the domain is fixed, not instead of fixing it. TradesViz/TradeWink (2025-2026) independently reach the median: 'a capture ratio based on fewer than 30 trades ... is statistically unreliable, so median and outlier analysis should account for sample size' (pyfinagent has 32 -- barely at that floor). NEGATIVE RESULT: no 2024/2025/2026 trading source defines the degenerate cases; every vendor page still prescribes the plain arithmetic mean. The defect is a faithful implementation of the industry convention, and the convention is wrong -- so the statistics literature governs, not the trading literature.

The five promotion booleans are trades_ge_100 / psr_ge_95_sustained_30d / dsr_ge_95 / sr_gap_le_30pct / max_dd_within_tolerance -- capture and edge appear in NONE of them. backend/api/paper_trading.py:883 (_compute_learnings reconciliation) -- NOT AFFECTED, reads entry_price/exit_price only.

Optimizer, promoter, meta_evolution/alpha_velocity, Slack bot, BQ views/SQL -- ZERO occurrences of capture_ratio or edge_ratio (grep across backend/backtest/, backend/meta_evolution/, backend/slack_bot/, backend/agents/, *.sql). The test-fixture hit at tests/meta_evolution/test_alpha_velocity.py:130 is a generic components dict, not a real consumer.
VERDICT: no sizing, promotion, or trading decision reads these two metrics -- they are pure diagnostics. That materially lowers the blast radius of the fix.

Frontend: MfeMaeScatter.tsx:34,111,114,168 + frontend/src/lib/types.ts:766 + frontend/src/lib/api.ts:524. Must move to `number | null` and discriminate on PRESENCE -- otherwise (null * 100).toFixed(0) renders '0%', a fabricated 'captured nothing' (project_fabricated_safe_80_36 class).
corrections_to_main: Your prompt's premise that the frontend might ALSO double-scale is REFUTED, and you were right to demand it be checked separately: capture_ratio is dimensionless (percent/percent), so MfeMaeScatter.tsx:114's x100 is correct. There is exactly ONE defect and it is backend-side. Do not budget a frontend formatter fix -- but DO budget a frontend NULL-handling fix, which is a different change.

Your prompt says the 8 mfe==0 rows are 'included in the mean' -- correct, but the mechanism is worth stating precisely for the contract: they are not passed through as-is, they are ZERO-FILLED at paper_round_trips.py:97 (`... if mfe > 0 else 0.0`) before the mean ever sees them. So the row count is right and the VALUE is fabricated. That distinction changes the fix from 'filter the aggregation' to 'make the per-trade metric nullable at its birth site'.

Your prompt frames both blowups as the same problem. They are NOT symmetric, and treating them identically would ship a new bug: mae==0 rows are the BEST trades and excluding them (current behaviour at :1002) is a survivorship bias -- the fix must ADD them back, not filter them out like the mfe==0 rows. Exclude for capture, keep for edge.

The aggregation is in TWO places, not one. Your prompt names only backend/api/paper_trading.py. backend/services/paper_round_trips.py:157 carries an independent copy feeding /performance, and it is open audit finding 55.3 F-10 (avg_capture_ratio=-53.7, filed 2026-06, still unfixed). A single-site fix leaves the API emitting the blown-up number and leaves F-10 open.

Line numbers re-derived as requested and they have indeed moved: the endpoint is paper_trading.py:974-1047; the silent drop is :1002-1003; the two means are :1031 and :1032. Your '996-1032' span is correct.

There is a THIRD symptom on the same tile that your prompt does not mention: the leakage rule at :1027 tests capture < 0.4, which the fabricated 0.0 always passes -- so the n_leakers count is contaminated by all 8 mfe==0 rows. Fold it into 82.5 or it will survive the fix.

Do NOT let the fix touch pair_round_trips' pairing loop. paper_go_live_gate.py:131 derives the trades_ge_100 promotion boolean from len(pair_round_trips(trades)); a pairing change silently moves a go-live gate.

Prediction, not measurement: I did not re-run the 32 rows. The fixture numbers in the brief (capture median ~0.63, edge median >= 0.81) are DIRECTIONAL predictions with stated derivations. Per feedback_measure_dont_assert_claims, the executor must re-measure them under the chosen MIN_MFE_PCT before writing any of them into immutable verification criteria -- and per feedback_immutable_criteria_must_be_green_able, do not pin an exact numeric equality you have not run.

OUT OF SCOPE, QUEUE SEPARATELY (per feedback_queue_discovered_defects_in_masterplan): paper_round_trips.py:147-152 mixes units -- profit_factor is built from realized_pnl_usd while avg_win_pct/avg_loss_pct/expectancy_pct are built from realized_pnl_pct. That is the OTHER half of 55.3 F-10 (profit_factor=0.0229 alongside win_rate=0.64). I did not measure it; it is a lead, not a verdict.

Gate honesty: 7 sources read in full (floor 5), 26 URLs, recency scan performed. Two disclosed gaps -- (a) QuantifiedStrategies, the canonical Sweeney-anchored page, is bot-blocked to BOTH WebFetch and curl+tag-strip, and Sweeney's Campaign Trading (1996) is offline-only, so the Sweeney definition is carried at second hand; (b) arXiv:1409.4896 was abstract-only (ar5iv 307-redirects) and is filed as snippet-only, NOT counted toward the gate. The brief also exceeds the moderate tier's 700-word target -- the overrun is evidence tables plus the enumerated degenerate-case spec you asked for, disclosed rather than trimmed.
